means: One long-lived computer where your agents work.
Where a dropped computer waits.
A small part of Silo that runs inside the computer.
The edge of a computer.
One way through the boundary.
Facts and reports are written once, and together they are the record.
One thing Silo saw itself, from outside the computer. Written once.
One thing a program inside the computer told Silo. Written once. An agent with full access can interfere with it.
What a classifier, or you, think about facts and reports. It can be wrong, and it says whose it is.
Whatever gives an opinion.
A rule is triggered by a fact. It is exact, and it may do anything you wrote in it.
A precaution is triggered by a report or an opinion. It can be wrong, so it takes only protective actions.
Said of an action after which a computer can do something it could not just before.
Said of an action that ends or erases something, and that cannot be undone.
Said of an action that grants nothing and destroys nothing. A wrong one costs only time.
The request waits at the boundary for the answer.
Nothing waits.
One launch of an agent program, and every process descended from it.
A sequence of turns with one model.
One reply of the model.
One thing the reply asked for.
What it left: processes, file changes, connections.
The core piece of Silo. The app, the command line and every tool only talk to it.
Rules, a computer, or both, added to Silo through a manifest.
What an extension says of itself: the rules it adds, the recipe of its computer, what wakes that computer and the tools it may use.
A view in the app that an extension creates through a tool, and that the app draws.
Said of an extension: what makes its computer run something. "Triggered" is kept for a rule or a precaution.
One thing that asks to cross the boundary. It may wait there for an answer.
A text that says how to make a computer.
A command run in a fork or in a fresh computer, with an end.
Told to Silo, not seen by it. Said of every report, and of a result computed from reports.
An opinion about a report: the facts agree with it. The report stays unverified.
An opinion about a report: the facts disagree with it.
